conviction_note: This print trades on the regulatory update 12 days before the 2026-11-22 PDUFA, not on the P&L. No sourced, unpriced fact settles what the release will say about the FDA review, so p_up is 52 on a 20% absolute move (implied 44.8%, but the ATM spread is 69% of mid; last print +58% on a regulatory pivot; median 8.7%). The +2.5 findings sum leans slightly positive: a very crowded short (34% of shares out, 43.6% of float) and a management team that controls its message with no Q&A, set against a 35% 20-day run-up into a bland-update risk. The scaled number is smaller than the sum because the sign of the regulatory language is unknowable from here.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus -$0.61 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-04, https://finviz.com/news/415722/capricors-q3-report-must-show-whether-its-narrower-fda-path-for-deramiocel-is-holding). Only one source, and there is no product revenue and no formal guidance. The real bar is qualitative: does the BLA review sound on track for 2026-11-22 (labeling talks, Form 483 closed, no new FDA requests)? H.C. Wainwright (Neutral) expects a CRL. The 2026-08-24 Benzinga piece puts consensus at Buy with a $38.25 average target over 10 analysts, against a $9.28 spot. Every finding is capped small because the bar is unsourced as a number.
positioning_check: Short interest: 19.86M shares (prior month 18.83M), 43.61% of float, 34.16% of shares outstanding, 5.5 days to cover, per stockanalysis.com (page updated 2026-11-10; settlement date not shown) https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/capr/statistics/. Older aggregator readings ran 20-37% of float (Apr-Aug 2026). Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline, so there is no directional statement from the options. Put/call open interest is 0.11 on 17,058 contracts, so the book is call-heavy. ATM IV is 561% with the spread at 69% of mid. Tape: +12.6% over 5 days and +34.9% over 20 days, -73.7% from the 52-week high. Stocktwits retail sentiment was 'bullish' with high message volume on 2026-11-03, and one user there attributed the rally to short covering. Crowded short plus call-heavy retail: both a squeeze and a sell-the-news are live mechanisms.

findings.finding: The short is very crowded: 19.86M shares short, 43.6% of float and 34.2% of shares outstanding, 5.5 days to cover, and rising (18.83M the prior month). That is going into an amc update whose only plausible positive content (labeling discussions, Form 483 closed, review 'on track') would force covering against 3.3M shares of average daily volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At the Q2 print (2026-08-13) a regulatory-path update into a heavily shorted, collapsed stock moved +57.96% close to close (+67% after hours). The 2026-08-24 PDUFA extension moved +14%. On 2026-11-03, a retail user credited short covering for a +14% day.
findings.why_not_priced: The short has grown into the event rather than covered, so shorts are positioned for a CRL on 11-22, not for a good-sounding update on 11-10. If it were priced, short interest would be falling into the print and the stock would not be gapping on soft news like an investigator letter. The asymmetry exists only if the update leans positive, which is unknown.
findings.independence: The Stocktwits 2026-11-03 article reports a retail claim of short covering (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/capr-stock-rises-as-clinical-trial-investigators-write-to-fda-urging-approval-for-deramiocel/cNGX1b1R9d0). It is an anecdote from a different source.

findings.finding: The stock is +34.9% over 20 days and +12.6% over 5 days into the print. The only new company content since 2026-10-05 is the 2026-11-09 AHA award PR; the rest of the rally came from third-party items (the investigator letter, a webinar). So a status-quo 'continuing to work with the FDA' update risks sell-the-news, and call open interest dominates (P/C OI 0.11).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-10-05 release of positive OLE data fell about 6.1% after the 10.5% conference-day run (catalyst tracker cited in search). Of 7 prior prints, 5 rose; 2026 Q4/Q1 prints with no regulatory change were -8.7% and -3.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself the market pricing hope. The open question is whether the release adds anything, and the PR list shows the company has said nothing on the review since 2026-08-24. If the market expected a bland update, the stock would not have run 35% into it.
findings.independence: The baseline tape (run_up_20d 34.88%, run_up_5d 12.62%) and the Stocktwits 2026-11-03 article (+29% week) point the same way. They describe the same price path, not an independent signal. This finding is shrunk for the crowded-short finding above.

findings.finding: 28 HOPE-3 investigators wrote to FDA leadership on 2026-10-25 urging approval of deramiocel on upper-limb function and calling a further efficacy trial 'unethical'. This was made public on 2026-11-03 via lead investigator Craig McDonald's LinkedIn. It is soft evidence that the review faces external pressure toward approval on the refined indication.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose about 14% on 2026-11-03 when the letter surfaced, and 29% for the week.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the stock moved 14% on the day. The residual is whether management references FDA receptiveness on the call. Kept small.
findings.independence: The company's 2026-10-07 PPMD webinar data on heart and arm function (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/capr-stock-rises-nearly-5-as-capricor-presents-heart-data-for-deramiocel-ahead-of-november-fda-decision/cZDvAk3RBZO) is the same advocacy push from the investigator side.

findings.finding: The FDA's July 2026 BIMO inspection issued a Form 483 with one observation. In the Q2 release Capricor said it had responded and was awaiting feedback. The Q3 release is the first chance to say whether it is closed. A single-observation BIMO 483 normally closes; an open one 12 days before PDUFA would be a negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior 483 disclosure surprise on record for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The 483 was disclosed in August, but its status has not been updated publicly since. The Earnings Whispers preview names it as a watch item (https://finviz.com/news/415722/capricors-q3-report-must-show-whether-its-narrower-fda-path-for-deramiocel-is-holding). If the market had a view, the item would not still be listed as open in previews.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers 2026-11-04 preview flags the same item. It is a different source reading the same company disclosure.

findings.finding: The Nippon Shinyaku (NS Pharma) dispute is unresolved. Capricor withdrew its preliminary-injunction motion, expects arbitration to begin 'this fall', and is still seeking rescission of the US distribution agreement, which it calls economically unworkable on price. The Q3 release will update it, and an approval without a workable distributor caps launch economics.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measurable reaction to the May 2026 lawsuit filing in the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades on approval odds, and the commercial terms are a second-order item that previews mention only in passing. A ruling or settlement disclosure would be new.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/382059/capricor-therapeutics-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update) gives the same status. It is one company disclosure in two documents.

findings.finding: Cash fell from $318.1M (2025-12-31) to $237.9M (2026-06-30), about $40M a quarter, which implies roughly $195-200M at September 30. Runway is guided only to 'at least twelve months', excluding product sales and PRV proceeds. With the stock up 35% and a binary event in 12 days, a raise is possible, but no shelf or ATM activity has been filed since July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has been no financing event in the 2026 window to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: The burn is public. The only unpriced element is the timing of a raise, and nothing on EDGAR since 2026-07-14 (8-Ks for lease, AdCom, extension; 13Gs) points to one. Asked what money would buy: a launch, if approved, so a raise would be launch funding rather than distress. Kept near zero.
findings.independence: The EDGAR filing list shows no S-3, 424B or ATM since July (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001133869&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). It points against a raise.

findings.finding: Management controls the message. The Q2 2026 call ran without Q&A (the preview asks whether Q&A will be 'restored'), and the Nov 3 call notice mentions none. The Q2 update framed a regulatory pivot that moved the stock +58%, and the CEO has been categorical in public (she said there was 'no way' deramiocel gets only conditional approval). A scripted update 12 days before PDUFA is more likely to be framed constructively than to disclose bad news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (regulatory path update): +57.96%. Q3 2025: +11.51%. Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 (no new path): -8.74% and -3.78%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference about tone, not a fact about the FDA. The market can price it, and the run-up partly does. Kept small.
findings.independence: The Nov 3 call announcement (https://finviz.com/news/414304/capricor-therapeutics-to-report-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provide-recent-corporate-update-on-november-10) mentions no Q&A. The CEO's 'no way' conditional-approval quote is from Asianet Newsable (https://newsable.asianetnews.com/amp/markets/capr-stock-heads-for-best-week-in-nearly-a-month-ceo-says-no-way-deramiocel-gets-only-conditional-approval-articleshow-fq2uavm), with the date not verified.

findings.finding: Capricor put out a PR the day before the print: on 2026-11-09 its HOPE-3 Phase 3 cardiac results won an American Heart Association Outstanding Research Award in Pediatric Cardiology. That is an attempt to rehabilitate the cardiac data the AdCom voted 9-3 against.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and a day old, so mostly priced. It does not bear on the upper-limb indication under review. Small.

findings.finding: The Q3 P&L is irrelevant to the reaction. Consensus EPS is -$0.61 against -$0.70 in Q2. Opex rose to $42.9M in Q2, with non-deramiocel work on hold and launch prep slowed, so a narrower loss is plausible. The name has no product revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 EPS missed (-$0.70 vs -$0.58) and the stock rose 58% on the regulatory update. EPS does not drive this name.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/382059/capricor-therapeutics-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update) gives the cost actions.

outside_window.finding: The FDA action date on the deramiocel BLA (refined upper-limb indication, major amendment) is 2026-11-22. The AdCom voted 9-3 against cardiomyopathy effectiveness, the FDA briefing said HOPE-3 missed its prespecified endpoints, and H.C. Wainwright (Neutral) expects a CRL. This is the binary event, and it lands after the exit window.
NS Pharma arbitration outcome on rescission of the US distribution agreement. It is expected to begin in fall 2026, with no ruling date.

baseline_tension: Skew is null, so there is no options direction to beat. What I found splits the same way the tape does: a 35% run-up and call-heavy open interest argue sell-the-news, while 43.6% of float short argues squeeze. The net is near zero and p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): the run-up / sell-the-news finding moved from -1.5 to -1.0 because 43.6% of float is short.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the cash-burn / possible-raise finding moved from -0.5 to -0.3. What the money would buy is a launch, and no S-3 or ATM is on file.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): the EPS bar has one source, so all findings stay capped small. This was already applied in the draft and changed nothing further.
The scaled number (p_up 52, abs 20) is unchanged.
